title: Research Novelty Index
interpretation: Weighted rubric index (0–100), NOT calibrated probability of global novelty.

criteria.name: Prior-work originality
criteria.purpose: Distinguishable from closely related work in the originating field.

anchors.0: An essentially identical formulation/solution exists in originating field.
anchors.2: Meaningful but limited differences from established work.
anchors.3: Clear specific differentiation supported by close comparisons.
anchors.4: Highly distinctive contribution compared with the retrieved direct-domain prior work.

criteria.name: Scientific contribution
criteria.purpose: Specific new theoretical, methodological, conceptual or empirical knowledge.

anchors.1: Small implementation change with limited new inference.
anchors.2: Testable incremental extension or novel evaluation insight.
anchors.4: Potentially fundamental and clearly specified new contribution.

anchors.0: Problem adequately addressed by demonstrated prior work.
anchors.1: Claimed gap is weak or anecdotal.
anchors.2: Partial or contested resolution; some evidence of an open limitation.
anchors.3: Specific unresolved limitation corroborated by pertinent sources.
anchors.4: Well-established substantial open problem with defensible unresolved mechanism.

criteria.name: Cross-disciplinary novelty
criteria.purpose: Survives search for formal equivalents and transferable solutions in other disciplines.

anchors.0: Equivalent cross-domain solution exists, transfers without substantive changes.
anchors.1: Transfer well known; only cosmetic domain shift.
anchors.2: Analogous/transferable method exists; substantive assumptions differ.
anchors.3: Cross-domain transfer has major unresolved challenges or yields a genuinely new method.
anchors.4: Broad cross-domain search has not found a close solution and the distinctive structural contribution is clear.

criteria.name: Contextual originality
criteria.purpose: Novel constraints or setting generate generalisable knowledge, not merely a new dataset/place.

anchors.0: Context change without additional scientific question.
anchors.2: Context creates important but narrow validation requirements.
anchors.3: New assumptions or conditions enable generalisable insights.
anchors.4: New context introduces fundamental constraints that enable important new understanding.

decision_overrides: already_addressed if verified equivalent solution exists and no substantively novel contribution remains
provisional if material sources/cross-domain coverage are insufficient
human_review_required for decisive formal equivalence, clinical or patentability questions
